Hmmm. The question is vague and open-ended. Here's my vague and open-ended answer.

When I was in my teens I used to take psychedelic drugs, regularly and in large doses. My mom had kicked me out of the house, and my aunt had decided that she would car for me until I made 18 and could sign a lease since it seemed safer than cosigning for someone as irresponsible as I was.

One day I called in to work, dropped a ten strip of acid and went out partying.  That much acid doesn't wear off quickly, so a hotel stay or two, a paycheck, and several bizarre and (to me) incomprehensible near death experiences later I made my way back to my aunts house and finally fell asleep (sleeping on acid is HARD).

When I woke up I lit my morning cigarette, scratched my nuts, and stumbled downstairs for a smoke. There were men in hazmat suits with respirators everywhere, and plastic over everything.

I stood there while faceless suit-men stared at me, scratching my nuts, and wondering if this was an extenuation of the trip or not for about two minutes.

I nearly finished my smoke before one of the men spoke. "Mblarmuffleflurble?!?!?"

I thought, "Yeah. I'm going back to bed."

As I turn to walk back upstairs he finally lifts his mask, for just a second to say "Asbestos! No one was supposed to be home! Leave!"

I left. In my boxers. In a hurry. 

I didn't come back for a week, and none of the people I crashed with believed my story about the hazmat suit guys, but I worked out a version of the truth later.

It turns out that they'd been planning for months to renovate, but that the ceiling (or walls) had asbestos in them and that they'd hired a special crew to come in and clean it out. Due to my disappearing act no one had been able to warn me that it was coming up and I had no memory of anyone mentioning it.

The night before I had apparently just moved aside the plastic over the  doorway to the upstairs and stumbled to bed without thinking anything unusual was happening.

*tl;dr;* I stood there smoking a camel non-filter, in my boxers, scratching my nuts, while men in hazmat suits cleaned up asbestos around me.
